reviewer_issues.title: Novelty and differentiation from SSVC, CVSS v4.0, and existing approaches
reviewer_issues.reviewer_concern: Paper claims novelty in multi-factor prioritization, but SSVC formalizes decision trees integrating exploitation, exposure, and impact. How does VRS differ substantively from automating SSVC tiers? What advances beyond CVSS v4.0 environmental metrics?
reviewer_issues.root_cause: Manuscript does not explicitly compare VRS computational model against SSVC decision tree structure or CVSS v4.0 environmental metrics; positions construed as 'implement SSVC principles' rather than 'novel methodology'
required_actions: Conduct comparative evaluation: VRS vs. SSVC decision tree vs. CVSS v4.0 environmental scoring
Create Venn diagram: VRS (continuous linear) vs. SSVC (discrete branching) vs. CVSS v4.0 (numerical modifiers)
Document 3 distinct advantages of VRS: deterministic tie-breaking, parameter transparency, empirical weight tuning
Revise §2 (Related Work) with explicit differentiation
success_criteria: Explicit table: VRS vs. SSVC vs. CVSS v4.0 (≥4 metrics)
Documented advantages of deterministic tie-breaking
Revised manuscript §2 with clear differentiation

reviewer_issues.title: Circular author-generated benchmark labels
reviewer_issues.reviewer_concern: Reference labels are author-curated per SSVC rubric. SSVC incorporates KEV, EPSS, and exposure—same features in VRS. This creates construct circularity: high VRS performance reflects feature alignment, not empirical validation. How do you disentangle?
reviewer_issues.root_cause: Reference labels derived from SSVC decision tree which uses KEV/EPSS/N as inputs; VRS formula includes identical features; evaluation metric (Spearman ρ) measures construct consistency, not prediction validity
required_actions: Recruit 3-5 independent security professionals for CVE triage annotation
Recompute Spearman ρ using independent consensus labels
Conduct ANOVA comparing performance across label sources (author SSVC vs. independent vs. SOC telemetry if available)
Reframe paper results: 'construct consistency evaluation' NOT 'empirical breach prediction'
Revise abstract and claims throughout manuscript
success_criteria: 3+ independent annotations per CVE with κ ≥0.60
Spearman ρ table: author_ssvc vs. independent vs. telemetry
Clear quantification: X% of VRS gain from SSVC construct, Y% from feature predictiveness
Manuscript reframed as 'construct alignment' (C1) + 'feature predictiveness' (C2)

reviewer_issues.title: Unfair baselines lacking network exposure and asset criticality
reviewer_issues.reviewer_concern: Baselines 1–4 operate only on vulnerability attributes (C, E, K), while VRS includes environmental context (N, A). This informational asymmetry makes baseline comparison unfair. VRS superiority may reflect data availability, not method quality.
reviewer_issues.root_cause: SSVC decision tree requires exposure + impact; VRS mirrors this structure; baselines designed as 'CVSS v3.1 industry standard' (lacking environmental context); no fair information-symmetric comparison
required_actions: Create context-augmented baselines: CVSS/EPSS/Combo with access to N and A
Run controlled comparison: 4 methods × 2 context settings (8 configurations)
Quantify context contribution: Δρ for each baseline with/without context
Promote VRS (No Context) ablation to primary result (vulnerable-only comparison)
Document information-symmetric fairness in manuscript
success_criteria: 8-method comparison table with ρ values
Clear demonstration: 'Context accounts for 0.06–0.08 ρ; VRS formula 0.01–0.03 ρ'
Manuscript revised: 'When environmental context available to all, VRS and symmetric baselines comparable (ρ ≥0.88)'

reviewer_issues.title: Unjustified VRS weights
reviewer_issues.reviewer_concern: Default weights (w_C=0.25, w_E=0.20, w_K=0.20, w_N=0.20, w_A=0.15) appear arbitrary. No justification or sensitivity analysis provided. How were these chosen? What is the impact of weight variation?
reviewer_issues.root_cause: Weights defined as 'exploratory' in manuscript but no derivation shown; no weight sensitivity study or optimization procedure described
required_actions: Conduct grid search over weight space (simplex): each w ∈ [0, 1], Σw=1.0
Conduct Bayesian optimization (Gaussian process) for efficient search
Evaluate generalization: optimized weights on 41-CVE vs. 500-CVE
Compare to default: 'default weights near-optimal (within 0.01 ρ)' OR 'optimized weights yield 0.03 ρ improvement but overfit'
Justify weight choice in manuscript (empirical optimization, robustness, or exploration rationale)
success_criteria: Grid search and Bayesian optimization executed; best-found weights documented
Comparison table: Default vs. optimized on both 41-CVE and 500-CVE
Clear statement: 'Default weights are near-optimal OR represent conservative choice'

reviewer_issues.title: Insufficient guardrail evaluation
reviewer_issues.reviewer_concern: Evidence validation covers 8 injection patterns on MockLLM and 5 adversarial banners on live Llama-3.1-8B. This is limited. How does it generalize to unknown attack vectors, multilingual prompts, or frontier models? What is the false negative rate?
reviewer_issues.root_cause: MockLLM is deterministic (not stochastic); only 5 adversarial banners tested (small attack surface); no frontier model testing; no multi-turn or multilingual attacks; false positive rate not measured
required_actions: Curate adversarial attack corpus: OWASP Top 10 LLM Injections (20–30 patterns)
Create multilingual attack corpus: CJK, Arabic, Russian, Hindi variants (10–15 patterns)
Conduct multi-turn red-teaming (5–10 turns per attack) on frontier models
Generate legitimate explanations on 41-CVE benchmark; measure false positive rate
Evaluate on ≥3 models: Llama-3.1-8B, GPT-4, Claude 3.5 Opus (if API access available)
Revise RQ3 framing: 'tested on known patterns' NOT 'proof of jailbreak resistance'
dependencies: Requires API access to frontier models
success_criteria: Evaluation on ≥3 models
Adversarial corpus: ≥20 injection patterns, ≥10 multilingual variants, multi-turn scenarios
Confusion matrix for each model; true positive rate ≥85%, false positive rate <5%
Manuscript revised: 'tested on known patterns', not 'proof of jailbreak resistance'

reviewer_issues.title: Unclear RAG retrieval implementation
reviewer_issues.reviewer_concern: Paper mentions 'retrieval-augmented generation' but does not explain what is retrieved, from where, or how. Are you retrieving from NVD, EPSS, KEV, or external databases? Is retrieval deterministic or learned? No retrieval metrics reported.
reviewer_issues.root_cause: Manuscript describes RAG as 'evidence validation layer' but underspecifies retrieval mechanism; retrieval.py minimal (47 lines); dual-mode (exact+keyword) but no quality metrics; no comparison to alternatives
required_actions: Document current retrieval mechanism: sources (NVD, EPSS, KEV), algorithm (exact+keyword)
Implement BM25 retrieval (rank_bm25 library)
Implement embedding-based retrieval (SentenceTransformer: 'all-MiniLM-L6-v2')
Benchmark: precision@5, recall@5, MRR, latency for all three methods
If embedding-based superior, design plan for vector database integration
success_criteria: Documented retrieval mechanism: source data, algorithm, quality metrics
Comparison table: 3 methods × 5 metrics
Clear statement: 'Dual-mode achieves X% precision, Y% recall; embedding-based improves recall to Z%'

reviewer_issues.title: Missing explanation quality evaluation
reviewer_issues.reviewer_concern: Paper claims RAG provides 'intuitive triaging assistance' but reports no metrics on explanation quality: factuality, length, usefulness. How is explanation quality measured? Are longer explanations better? How do you evaluate faithfulness to evidence?
reviewer_issues.root_cause: Manuscript focuses on guardrails (injection rejection) but not explanation quality; no metrics for informativeness, length, or utility; evaluate_rag.py tests schema validity and injection, not content
required_actions: Define explanation quality rubric: factuality (0–10), actionability (0–10), length (0–10), source citation (0–10)
Implement automated evaluation: fact-checking, action specificity, token counting, citation extraction
Conduct human review on sample of 10 CVEs: 3 experts score 0–10 scale
Measure inter-rater agreement (Fleiss κ); correlation with automated scores
Compare: mean quality score with evidence vs. without (hallucination baseline)
success_criteria: Explanation quality rubric defined (4+ dimensions, explicit scoring)
Automated evaluation pipeline implemented
Human review on ≥10 CVEs; κ ≥0.60
Mean scores table (factuality, actionability, length, citations) for all 41 CVEs
Comparison: quality with evidence vs. without

reviewer_issues.title: Small benchmark and lack of confidence intervals/statistical tests
reviewer_issues.reviewer_concern: The 41-CVE benchmark is small. No confidence intervals or statistical significance tests provided. NDCG=1.0000 appears perfect but could be artifact of small size. How do you know results are statistically significant?
reviewer_issues.root_cause: 41-CVE benchmark manually curated; small N limits generalizability; results reported as point estimates; no statistical significance testing; perfect NDCG@10 likely due to ceiling effects
required_actions: Implement bootstrap resampling (1000 resamples) for each method and metric
Compute 95% confidence intervals (percentile method: 2.5th, 97.5th percentiles)
Conduct paired t-tests: VRS vs. each baseline; apply Bonferroni correction (α=0.05/4=0.0125)
Compute Cohen's d effect sizes
Report all results as 'Mean [95% CI]' format
Explain ceiling effects: '15 Tier 1 items in 41; any top-10 all Tier 1 → NDCG@10=1.0'
Promote multi-budget and Spearman to primary findings
success_criteria: Bootstrap CI computed for Spearman and NDCG (all methods)
Paired t-tests with Bonferroni correction; p-values and effect sizes
Results table: 'Mean [95% CI]' for all metrics
Clear statement: 'VRS ρ significantly exceeds CVSS (p<0.001, d=1.2) but overlaps with EPSS'

reviewer_issues.title: Temporal leakage due to later EPSS/KEV snapshots
reviewer_issues.reviewer_concern: Manuscript uses EPSS snapshot from 2026-10-13 and KEV snapshot from 2026-10-13. If manuscript submission was earlier, this introduces temporal leakage: future ground truth (later EPSS/KEV status) is used to evaluate past predictions. This is a form of look-ahead bias.
reviewer_issues.root_cause: EPSS and KEV snapshots dated 2026-10-13; manuscript submission date unclear; if before 2026-10-13, temporal leakage occurs; no discussion of snapshot provenance or temporal alignment
required_actions: Confirm manuscript submission date; compare to 2026-10-13 snapshot date
If temporal leakage: acquire historical EPSS/KEV snapshots (T-1 month, T-2 months)
Re-evaluate VRS using time-aligned snapshots; compute ranking stability (Kendall τ)
Report both snapshot-date results (if applicable) and document temporal dimension
If no leakage: document timeline alignment in appendix
success_criteria: Explicit confirmation: submission date and snapshot dates aligned/misaligned
If leakage: results using time-aligned snapshots
Ranking stability metric: Kendall τ between snapshots (should be >0.9)

reviewer_issues.title: Possible lack of independence in 500-CVE experiment
reviewer_issues.reviewer_concern: The 500-CVE corpus includes the 39 curated benchmark CVEs plus 461 sampled from cves/2023/0xxx, cves/2024/0xxx. How is this not training-on-test data? The 39 curated CVEs were labeled; are they also in the 500-CVE set? This violates experimental independence.
reviewer_issues.root_cause: 500-CVE corpus explicitly includes the 39 curated benchmark CVEs with author-assigned labels; potential for overfitting: VRS weights may be tuned on 39, then 'validated' on same 39 within 500-CVE set
required_actions: Verify data composition: confirm 39 labeled CVEs included in 500-CVE corpus
Create held-out 461-CVE set (excluding labeled 39)
Re-evaluate on held-out set; compare performance to current 500-CVE results
Quantify overfitting: 'R@25 on 500 (with labeled 39): X%; R@25 on 461 held-out: Y%'
If performance delta <5%: strong independence; if >5%: potential overfitting concern
success_criteria: Explicit confirmation: 39 labeled CVEs included/excluded from 500-CVE corpus
If included: held-out 461-CVE results alongside current 500-CVE
Performance comparison table
Manuscript clarified: experimental independence documented

reviewer_issues.title: Missing actionable metrics
reviewer_issues.reviewer_concern: Paper reports NDCG, Precision, Recall, Spearman correlation. These are ranking metrics, not actionable security metrics. What about false positive rate (over-flagging low-risk CVEs), false negative rate (missing real exploits), or timeliness (time-to-remediation)? How do you measure real-world impact?
reviewer_issues.root_cause: Evaluation focuses on ranking accuracy (academic metrics) not operational security impact; no false positive/negative metrics; no temporal aspect (time-to-remediation); paper claims 'help SOC analysts' but does not evaluate analyst productivity
required_actions: Define false positives/negatives in prioritization context (TP/FP/FN/TN)
Implement SOC triage simulation: analyst remediates top-K CVEs under budget constraint
Measure outcomes: Precision (true positives / alerts), Recall (true positives / total exploits), F1
Measure alert fatigue: Precision@K (% actionable), false positive rate
Measure early warning: days from VRS top-K to KEV listing (average advancement vs. CVSS-only)
Evaluate across budgets K ∈ {10, 20, 50 CVEs}
success_criteria: False positive/negative rates computed for all methods
SOC simulation at budgets 10, 20, 50 CVEs
Results table: 'CVSS @ budget=50: 11/25 exploits (R=0.44); VRS @ budget=50: 25/25 (R=1.0)'
Early warning metric: 'VRS identifies exploits avg +X days before KEV vs. CVSS +Y days'
Manuscript revised: false positive/negative rates and operational impact reported

reviewer_issues.title: Missing literature and incorrect references
reviewer_issues.reviewer_concern: Bibliography incomplete. Missing references to recent work on CVSS v4.0, EPSS v2 (released 2024), newer RAG security papers (2024–2025). Some references to 2023 work already outdated. Are citations accurate?
reviewer_issues.root_cause: References.bib curated in mid-2026; may not include latest 2024–2025 work; EPSS v2 and CVSS v4.0 not cited; RAG security literature rapidly evolving
required_actions: Audit existing references: verify DOI accuracy, page numbers, author names
Search literature: 'CVSS v4', 'EPSS v2', 'RAG security', 'prompt injection' (2023–2026, focus 2024–2025)
Identify 5–10 high-impact recent works; add BibTeX entries
Update §2 (Related Work) with citations to CVSS v4.0, EPSS v2, recent RAG security work
Spot-check 10 random citations for accuracy
success_criteria: Bibliography audit completed: 5–10 recent works identified
Reference accuracy checked: 10+ citations verified
§2 updated: explicit reference to CVSS v4.0, EPSS v2, recent RAG security

reviewer_issues.title: Nmap/CPE matching not adequately evaluated
reviewer_issues.reviewer_concern: Paper mentions CPE normalization and Nmap integration but provides minimal evaluation. How accurate is CPE matching? What is false negative rate (missed CVEs)? How does it handle version ambiguity (e.g., 'Apache 2.4' vs. '2.4.49')? No test results provided.
reviewer_issues.root_cause: cve_matcher.py implements CPE normalization but no standalone evaluation; tests basic functionality but not accuracy; no benchmark for CPE matching quality; version ambiguity handling not documented
required_actions: Create ground-truth validation set: 20 real Nmap XML outputs with manually annotated applicable CVEs
Evaluate CPE matching: precision, recall, F1 for each service
Analyze version ambiguity handling: 'Apache 2.4' (no patch version) vs. '2.4.49' (exact)
Measure latency: mean ms per service (target <100ms)
Compare matching strategies: exact CPE vs. fuzzy vs. manual version parsing
Document limitations (vendor naming inconsistencies, obfuscation)
success_criteria: Ground-truth validation set: 20 services with manual CVE annotations
CPE accuracy evaluated: Precision, Recall, F1 metrics
Results table: 'Apache 2.4.49: P=0.95, R=0.88; nginx 1.18: P=0.92, R=0.85'
Version ambiguity analysis: 'Recall drops from 0.88 to 0.72 without patch version'
Latency reported: mean per service (target <100ms)
